Closeout Report:
In this milestone, we focused on enhancing Weld, our universal wallet connector, by adding cross-chain capabilities and restructuring the library to be more modular and extensible. We re-architected the library into a set of core, reusable primitives, enabling us to extend Weld's powerful reactivity system to additional blockchains without much code duplication.
We also developed a suite of 150+ unit tests to ensure this foundational layer is robust, providing a stable base for Weld's current and future APIs.
Weld now supports wallet extensions and connections for the Cardano, Ethereum, Polygon, and Solana blockchains. With our new core primitives, we've streamlined the process for us and the community to add support for additional blockchains in the future.

Closeout Report:
In this milestone, we built upon our previous work to add Bitcoin support to Weld.
Similar to our other chain integrations, Weld now exports a new weldBtc instance with reactive stores that track installed extensions, monitor connected wallet attributes and balances. These stores also offer a unified interface for sending transfers, signing transactions, and retrieving wallet contents. This Bitcoin integration works with any frontend framework and includes first-class bindings for React.
Unlike Cardano's standardized wallet APIs, the Bitcoin ecosystem features diverse and non-standardized extension interfaces. We therefore focused our initial integration on two popular and well-documented wallets: XVerse and Unisat.
Additionally, we plan to add support for the WBIP-004 Web Providers standard once it gains wider adoption. Currently, only a handful of wallets have implemented WBIP-004, and even among those, there are some inconsistencies in how the standard is applied.
